skill.name: agent-fungibility
skill.description: Guidance for using fungible, interchangeable agents in multi-agent software development workflows.
skill.summary: Plan software work so any agent can take the next ready task and recover from failures.
skill.author: Dicklesworthstone

content.value_statement: Multi-agent software projects can stall when agents have fixed roles and fragile handoffs. This skill teaches a shared-task workflow where any Claude, Codex, or Claude Code agent can take the next ready bead.
actual_capabilities: Explains why interchangeable agents can reduce bottlenecks in software projects.
Compares fungible agents with permanent specialist roles.
Describes using BV commands to select the next ready bead.
Shows how a shared initial prompt can align multiple agents.
Outlines recovery when an agent session fails or loses context.
Identifies cases where specialized agent roles may still be useful.
limitations: It is workflow guidance, not an automation package.
It assumes BV, NTM, Agent Mail, and bead tracking already exist.
It does not install tools or verify local command availability.
Example commands should be reviewed before use in sensitive repositories.

use_cases.title: Scale a Coding Swarm
use_cases.description: Turn a planned backlog into ready beads so many agents can work without permanent role assignments.

use_cases.title: Recover Failed Sessions
use_cases.description: Replace a crashed or confused agent by using shared project context and current bead state.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Coordination Models
use_cases.description: Compare fungible swarms with specialized roles before designing a multi-agent development workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain agent fungibility for a software team using Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Include the main benefits and when not to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Swarm
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a starter workflow for three fungible agents using beads, BV triage, and Agent Mail. Keep setup steps concise.

prompt_templates.title: Recover a Stalled Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent swarm status and propose how to replace failed agents without role mapping. Focus on bead state and shared context: [status].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Large Swarm Protocol
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a scalable fungible-agent operating model for [project]. Include task intake, readiness rules, communication norms, failure recovery, and governance checks.

output_examples.input: I need to start five agents on a backlog with mixed coding and testing work.
output_examples.output: Use one shared starting context, convert the plan into dependency-aware beads, and let every agent choose the next ready bead. Add agents without permanent roles.

output_examples.input: One Claude Code session failed during a refactor.
output: Treat bead state as the source of truth.
Start a replacement session with the same project context.
Have the new agent inspect active beads and either resume or choose ready work.

output_examples.input: Our team wants separate tester, backend, and reviewer agents.
output_examples.output: Use specialized roles only when the role structure creates value. For normal software delivery, keep agents interchangeable and encode needs in each bead.

best_practices: Put project context, constraints, and acceptance criteria into the plan before creating beads.
Use shared readiness rules so every agent can choose work without central assignment.
Keep communication brief and make state changes visible in beads and agent mail.
anti_patterns: Assigning permanent specialist roles before the backlog proves they are needed.
Letting agents wait for handoffs when a ready bead is available.
Using a shared initial prompt without reviewing commands for the current repository.

faq.question: What is agent fungibility?
faq.answer: It means each agent can handle any ready task instead of holding a permanent specialist role.

faq.question: Which tools does this skill mention?
faq.answer: It mentions Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Amp, Cursor, BV, NTM, and Agent Mail.

faq.question: Does this skill install or run automation?
faq.answer: No. It is guidance and command examples for a workflow that the user controls.

faq.question: When are specialized agents better?
faq.answer: They can help when structured debate or distinct perspectives are the main purpose of the system.

faq.question: Can it work with mixed agent products?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill describes using different agent products as interchangeable workers on the same bead queue.

faq.question: What should I review before use?
faq.answer: Review local BV, NTM, Agent Mail setup, command examples, repository permissions, and any data shared with agents.
